name: spine-widened-invariants-audit
body:
Widened-invariant sweep of the spine-backfill spec, after I1-I5 were already clean. Results (counts: before -> after; I6/I7/I9 re-counted by the represents pass appended at the end):

I1-I5 unchanged and still clean.
I6 person/user linkage (REVISED by the represents pass — see the appended section): initially represents edges 0 -> 0; persons all `uses` the system (3), users all `contains` requirements (2), and the model did not use represents (recorded at the time in the now-retired global.note.represents-unused). The human gate ruled represents mandatory and the actor chain was added: I6 is now represents edges 0 -> 6, with every User and Person paired through user -> entity -> person.
I7 domain structure: entities in a group 9/9 -> 12/12 (the three actor entities join the new domain.group.actors); groups with >=1 entity 4/6 -> 5/7 (upgrade and validation have none — justified as capability groups, see domain.note.group-less-domains-audit); uncontained values 1 -> 0 (item-context now in domain.group.templating); uncontained services 1 -> 0 (render-sections, CLOSED by the follow-up below).
I8 solution structure: 30/30 components contained by a container; 4/4 containers contained by solution.system.kalide; 30/30 components have >=1 implemented-by; 30/30 have >=1 realised-by. Clean before and after.
I9 tier-1 structure: 3 stakeholders, 2 -> 3 users (requirements.user.maintainer added), 81 requirements, 81/81 requirements reachable from a stakeholder (I4). Users cannot be contained by a Stakeholder — the binary refuses Stakeholder->User; they are anchored the schema-legal way (stakeholder -> every user-rooted requirement, already recorded in requirements.note.spine-stakeholder-reachability). The maintainer user's roots (distribution, deck-library-upgrade) were already stakeholder-reachable, so no new anchor was needed.
I10 service anchors: 13/13 services realised-by a solution node; 13/13 driven by >=1 requirement. Clean.
I5+ integrity: no dangling authored endpoints; no contains or depends-on cycles; every constraint attaches-to resolves; all authored edge kinds are schema-legal (contains, drives, realised-by, implemented-by, depends-on, details, uses person->system, calls service->service, publishes/subscribes service->event, represents user->entity and entity->person).

Net change this round: one contains edge (domain.group.templating -> domain.value.item-context), plus notes recording the ambiguous/open items. [autonomous]

Follow-up [with user]: the last open I7 item (render-sections containment) was decided at the human gate — added contains domain.group.presentation -> domain.service.render-sections (option (a1) rendering-pipeline grouping, over (a2) domain.group.templating), closing the sweep. render-sections remains realised-by solution.component.renderer and driven by five requirements. Re-verified: uncontained services 0/13, no contains cycle, I1-I5 still clean. See domain.note.group-less-domains-audit finding (2).

Represents pass [with user] (supersedes the I6/I7/I9 counts above): the human gate ruled `represents` mandatory. A direct user->person edge is refused by the binary (allowed shapes: requirements.user -> domain.entity; domain.entity -> solution.person), so the actor chain was added — domain.group.actors plus domain.entity.{deck-author,template-author,maintainer}, requirements.user.maintainer, and 6 represents edges (3 x user->entity, 3 x entity->person). Re-verified on this branch: I6 represents 0 -> 6, every User represented by a Person (3/3) and every Person represented by a User (3/3), 0 gaps both directions; I7 entities in a group 12/12, uncontained services 0/13; I9 3 users, 81/81 requirements stakeholder-reachable; I1-I5, I8 and I10 unchanged and clean; no contains or depends-on cycles, no dangling endpoints; all six actor-chain edges are schema-legal. See global.note.represents-actor-tier and domain.note.actor-entities.

Realised-by correction [with user] (post-dates the counts above): actor entities are anchored to the solution tier by `represents` -> solution.person.*, NOT by `realised-by`. The earlier actor-tier realised-by edges (domain.entity.deck-author and domain.entity.template-author -> solution.container.cli-binary, domain.entity.maintainer -> solution.container.release-pipeline, domain.group.actors -> solution.system.kalide) asserted that a person/role is realised by the CLI binary or the release pipeline — false — and had been added only to satisfy an 'every entity has a realised-by' count; they have been removed. The realised-by invariant applies to requirement-driven domain nodes (those a Requirement `drives`); actor entities are identity anchors, not requirement-driven, and are exempt. No audit count changes: I7 (containment), I8 (solution containers/components) and I10 (services) never depended on actor-tier realised-by edges. Re-verified after the removal: I6 represents 3/3 users and 3/3 persons, 0 gaps both directions; requirement spine 81/81; stakeholder reachability 81/81; no contains or depends-on cycles, no dangling endpoints. See global.note.represents-actor-tier and domain.note.actor-entities.
